Randomly sample records from FASTQ file(s)

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
random_sample_fastq.Rd

Randomly samples a specified number of records from one or two FASTQ files and writes the selected records to output file(s). The input files are processed in chunks to avoid loading the entire files into memory.

Usage

random_sample_fastq(
  fastq1,
  fastq2 = NULL,
  outfile1,
  outfile2 = NULL,
  n = 1e+06,
  randseed = NULL,
  check_pair_counts = TRUE,
  chunk_records = 25000,
  compress_method = "R",
  pigz_path = NULL,
  quiet = TRUE,
  num_threads = 0,
  fast_count = TRUE,
  total_reads = NULL,
  log_file = NULL
)

Arguments

fastq1

Character string giving the path to the first FASTQ file. Files ending in .gz are treated as gzip-compressed.

fastq2

Optional character string giving the path to the second FASTQ file. This is typically the mate FASTQ file for paired-end sequencing. If supplied, it must contain the same number of records as fastq1.

outfile1

Character string giving the path to the output file for fastq1. A filename ending in .gz produces gzip-compressed output.

outfile2

Character string giving the path to the output file for fastq2. A filename ending in .gz produces gzip-compressed output. This argument is ignored if fastq2 is NULL.

n

Integer specifying the number of records to sample. Sampling is performed without replacement. Defaults to 1e6.

randseed

Optional integer used to initialize the random number generator with set.seed. Setting this argument makes the sampling reproducible.

check_pair_counts

Logical indicating whether to verify that fastq1 and fastq2 contain the same number of reads. Defaults to TRUE. When FALSE, fastq2 is not counted, which can substantially reduce the processing time for large paired-end FASTQ files. Disabling this check assumes that the forward and reverse FASTQ files contain the same number of reads and should therefore be used only when this has been verified beforehand.

chunk_records

Integer specifying the maximum number of FASTQ records to process in each chunk. Each FASTQ record consists of four lines. Defaults to 2.5e4.

compress_method

Character string specifying the compression method used by fast_copy when input file(s) are copied directly, without sampling (i.e. n > number of reads) Supported values are "R", "pigz", and "gzip". Defaults to "R".

pigz_path

Optional path to the pigz executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.pigz_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

quiet

Logical indicating whether progress messages should be suppressed. Defaults to TRUE.

num_threads

Integer specifying the number of threads to use when compress_method = "pigz". A value of 0 uses all detected CPU cores. Defaults to 0.

fast_count

Logical value controlling the counting method. When TRUE on Linux, shell commands are used for faster counting. When FALSE, the chunk-based R implementation is used on all operating systems. This argument is passed to count_reads.

total_reads

Integer or NULL. The total number of sequences in the input file, if already known (e.g. from a pre-computed value or an info file). If NULL (the default), the function will count the sequences in the file itself, which can be slow for large files. Supplying total_reads skips this counting step and uses the given value directly, so it is the caller's responsibility to ensure it is correct.

log_file

Character string specifying the path to the CSV log file. The path is resolved with the following priority:

  1. the log_file argument, if explicitly provided by the user;

  2. the vtamR.log_file option set with options(vtamR.log_file = ...), if set;

  3. "vtamR_log.csv" in the current working directory, used as a last resort if neither of the above is set.

To disable logging entirely, set log_file = NA.

Value

Invisibly returns the number of records sampled. If n >= total, the total number of records in the input file is returned instead.

Details

When two FASTQ files are provided, the same set of record indices is used for both files, preserving the pairing between R1 and R2 reads. The two input files are checked to ensure that they contain the same number of records when check_pair_counts == TRUE.

For single-end FASTQ data, fastq2 can be omitted.

If the requested number of records is greater than or equal to the total number of records, no sampling is performed. Instead, the input file(s) are copied directly to the output file(s) using fast_copy.

The function first calls sample_fastq_indices to determine the total number of records and generate a random set of record indices. The selected indices are shared between fastq1 and fastq2 when paired-end files are provided.

Selected records are extracted using extract_fastq_records. Input FASTQ files are processed in chunks of chunk_records records, limiting memory usage for large sequencing datasets.

Both compressed (.gz) and uncompressed FASTQ files are supported. Input and output compression can differ; for example, an uncompressed FASTQ file can be sampled and written as a gzip-compressed file.

If n is greater than or equal to the number of records, the input files are not read record by record. Instead, they are copied directly to the output using fast_copy. In paired-end mode, both input files are copied.

See also

sample_fastq_indices, extract_fastq_records, fast_copy, count_reads

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Randomly sample 10,000 reads from a single FASTQ file
random_sample_fastq(
  fastq1 = "reads.fastq",
  outfile1 = "sample.fastq",
  n = 10000
)

# Randomly sample paired-end reads
random_sample_fastq(
  fastq1 = "reads_R1.fastq.gz",
  fastq2 = "reads_R2.fastq.gz",
  outfile1 = "sample_R1.fastq.gz",
  outfile2 = "sample_R2.fastq.gz",
  n = 10000,
  randseed = 123
)

# Sample reads and write compressed output
random_sample_fastq(
  fastq1 = "reads.fastq",
  outfile1 = "sample.fastq.gz",
  n = 10000,
  compress_method = "pigz",
  num_threads = 4
)
} # }
